players.product: Burn-in sockets for AI-server GPUs / ASICs / CPUs and automotive SoCs; entering the system-level test (SLT) market (test-socket commercialization in progress)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (April 2025 - March 2026) results: net sales JPY 42,540 million (up 11.7%), operating income JPY 6,164 million (up 16.6%), ordinary income JPY 6,482 million (up 19.0%), profit attributable to owners of parent JPY 5,233 million (up 32.7%). Segment sales: Semiconductor JPY 23,603 million, Life Science JPY 3,083 million, Digital Communication JPY 1,652 million, Energy Saving Solution JPY 14,201 million.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales JPY 42,540 million (+11.7%); operating income JPY 6,164 million (+16.6%); profit attributable to owners of parent JPY 5,233 million (+32.7%)

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor segment (IC test sockets, burn-in sockets) FY2026: sales JPY 23,603 million (up 46.4%), segment operating income JPY 4,974 million (up 225.2%); demand for server, automotive and mobile applications increased significantly. Management states it assumes server and automotive demand will keep rising over the medium term and expects AI-server sockets to increase for ASIC-related applications for hyperscalers in addition to major GPU makers; it is also focusing on technology development and business expansion of test sockets for future growth.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor sales JPY 23,603 million (+46.4%); segment operating income JPY 4,974 million (+225.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 R&D expenses JPY 1,698 million. Semiconductor R&D: IC sockets for higher density and high frequency; sockets with more pins and ultra-fine pitch for increasingly integrated mobile, AI and server semiconductors; production technology for high-mix low-volume sockets; for automotive semiconductors (sensors and processors for autonomous driving), long-life, high-current, high-heat-resistance and high-frequency socket solutions.

No external customer accounted for 10% or more of consolidated net sales in FY2026. FY2026 sales by customer location: United States JPY 10,780 million, Japan JPY 6,544 million, China JPY 6,096 million, Taiwan JPY 3,754 million, Singapore JPY 2,765 million, other Asia JPY 8,954 million, Europe JPY 3,003 million, other JPY 640 million; overseas sales are about 85% of consolidated net sales.
quarterly_data.figure: no customer at 10% or more of net sales; US sales JPY 10,780 million; overseas sales about 85%

quarterly_data.signal: Management priorities: monetize opportunities in the growing semiconductor market while accelerating investment to broaden the portfolio and avoid over-reliance on the Semiconductor business; each business to expand its domain and pursue niche-top, high-value positions to capture opportunities from the social implementation of AI; maximize free cash flow by monetizing upfront investments and concentrate resources in growth areas.

players.product: Plastic optical fiber lenses / lens arrays for optical transceivers (1.6T optical transceiver lenses in mass production), lens connectors, and CPO components for 3.2T / 6.4T (samples)

quarterly_data.signal: Digital Communication segment FY2026: sales JPY 1,652 million (down 66.2%), segment operating loss JPY 284 million (prior year: segment operating income JPY 2,484 million). Optical communication devices: mass production of next-generation products for high-end areas such as AI started, but sales were weak on a sharp decline in existing products and delayed launches of new products; LED diffusion lenses were weak on a stagnant LCD TV market. Orders received JPY 1,732 million (38.2% of the prior year), order backlog JPY 203 million (165.9%).
quarterly_data.figure: Digital Communication sales JPY 1,652 million (-66.2%); segment operating loss JPY 284 million; backlog JPY 203 million

quarterly_data.signal: Digital Communication R&D and outlook: the company develops optical products for transceivers supporting large data-center communications, focusing on lenses for high-end areas such as AI, and also develops high-function products other than transceiver optics and products in the opto-electronic integration field for faster data centers and next-generation mobile communication systems. Management expects new customers and new products to keep increasing over the medium term on data-center demand, centered on optical transceiver lenses and lens-connector products.
